page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-highmem-48 is a memory-focused compute instance engineered around the x86_64 CPU architecture. It provides 48 dedicated virtual CPUs paired with 384 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The configuration contains no dedicated hardware accelerators, providing zero GPUs, and includes no complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Storage architecture on the instance relies entirely on external network-attached volumes, as it features no local storage. This design isolates data persistence from the execution environment, requiring external block storage for operating system and application needs. By allocating 8 GB of memory per core, the machine provides substantial memory capacity without demanding an increase in core count, yielding balanced resource efficiency for memory-constrained deployments.

The hardware profile aligns with large-scale transactional databases, distributed in-memory caches, enterprise resource management platforms, and intensive extract-transform-load (ETL) data pipelines that require vast working sets in RAM without necessitating local drive scratchpads or accelerator hardware.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4d-highmem-48 is an x86_64 virtual instance configured with 48 dedicated vCPUs and 384 GB of system memory, providing an 8.0 GB per vCPU memory density. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, depending completely on network-attached storage volumes for system and data persistence, and features zero onboard GPUs. Without bundled physical drives or accelerator hardware, the platform focuses operational resources on substantial memory capacity relative to compute cores. This profile delivers cost efficiency for memory-heavy enterprise deployments by avoiding core overprovisioning solely to secure sufficient memory space. The instance is suited for large in-memory caching systems, memory-intensive database engines, large-scale data transformation jobs, and enterprise business applications.
